chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from more than one person, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: The best of your women are the women of Quraysh — the most kind toward their husbands, and the most merciful toward their children. The mujun toward her husband, the chaste toward others.
We said: And what is the mujun? He said: The one who does not withhold.

key_terms.ألطفهن: Kindness, gentleness, and tenderness toward husbands
key_terms.الحصان: Chastity and preservation of honor; modesty and restraint outside the marital relationship
key_terms.المجون: Playfulness/sensuality within marriage; a wife's willingness and responsiveness toward her husband

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the best women in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through al-Harith al-A'war from Imam Ali (AS), reports a saying of the Prophet (SAWW) praising Qurayshi women for two qualities: kindness (lutf) to their husbands and mercy (rahma) to their children. The hadith then introduces a third quality described as 'mujun' — playful intimacy within marriage — juxtaposed with 'hasan' (chastity/modesty) outside it. When asked to clarify, the Prophet explained mujun as refraining from withholding conjugal rights from one's husband. The term 'mujun' in classical Arabic carried connotations of boldness and playfulness; in this marital context it refers to a wife's willingness and responsiveness, while 'hasan' (preserved/chaste) indicates maintaining honor in public.
word_analysis: and the most merciful of them
